item.title: A8 Milano-Varese, Busto Arsizio exit closed for one night
item.description: Closure from 10 pm on 9 to 5 am on 10 September for work on safety barriers. Castellanza and Gallarate alternative exits.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Night closure of Busto Arsizio exit from 10:00 PM on 9 to 5:00 AM on 10 September - Inspection and maintenance work on safety barriers on A8 - Alternative exits: Castellanza or Gallarate depending on the direction
## Key facts - **What**: Closure of Busto Arsizio exit on A8 Milano-Varese - When: 10:00 PM Wednesday 9 September — 05:00 AM Thursday 10 September - Where: Busto Arsizio exit, province of Varese - Why: Inspection and maintenance work on safety barriers - Reopening: 05:00 AM Thursday 10 September - Who: Autostrade (manager of the section)
### The scheduled closure The Busto Arsizio exit will be blocked from 10:00 PM on Wednesday 9 to 5:00 AM on Thursday 10 September, both for those coming from Milan and for those arriving from the Varese direction. The closure was scheduled by Autostrade to allow inspection and maintenance activities of the safety barriers.
Unlike what it might seem, this is not a total interruption of the highway: only the Busto Arsizio exit will be inaccessible during the communicated time window. This means that vehicles in transit will necessarily have to change their route using the indicated alternative exits.
### Alternative routes for those coming from Milan Autostrade recommends two options for drivers arriving from Milan. The first, more direct, is to anticipate the exit at the Castellanza junction, which precedes Busto Arsizio in the direction of Varese. Alternatively, you can continue on the A8 towards Varese and exit at Gallarate, thus postponing the change of road by a few kilometers.
### Alternative routes for those coming from Varese For those arriving from the province of Varese, the priority indication is to anticipate the exit at Gallarate. Those who prefer not to exit in that area can continue towards Milan and use the Castellanza exit once past the Busto Arsizio closure point. ### Impacts on the mobility of border commuters
Ticino border crossers who daily travel on this route to Varesotto — one of the main poles of occupational attraction for those residing in the Canton of Ticino — will face a minor but not negligible disruption. A night closure represents a limited criticality in time, yet its operational management can influence the rhythms of evening return and morning departure for those who work across borders.
The province of Varese, with its industrial and commercial centres, absorbs a significant flow of commuters from Lugano, Mendrisio and the Ticino Riviera di Levante. For many of them, the A8 represents the main route of connection with the areas of use. A closure of a few hours, even if at night, requires a reorganization of the routes that can lengthen transit times.
### Travel strategy: choose in advance
The information advantage for those who move daily is predictability. As the closure is planned and communicated in advance, border crossers have the opportunity to plan their journey with awareness. Those who normally go out to Busto Arsizio will have to evaluate whether to opt for Castellanza (choice of anticipation) or for Gallarate (choice of continuation), based on their final location.
### The limited duration of the closure
The closing window — from 22 to 5 — affects the hours
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). Operational checklist for the night of September 9th
If you are a cross-border commuter who regularly travels on the A8 towards Varesotto, the night between September 9th and 10th requires some preparation:
Before leaving: - Check which exit you normally use (if it is Busto Arsizio, plan an alternative already in the car) - Consult an offline map of routes to Castellanza or Gallarate based on your destination - If the trip is in the evening (between 9 PM and 11 PM), consider leaving slightly earlier to avoid backtracking caused by sudden closures - Notify your employer if your return time may be affected
During the trip: - Stay focused: the need to change routes can distract from safe driving - If you use a navigator, enter the final destination and not just the usual exit, so the app will automatically suggest an alternative route - Castellanza exit: it is shorter, perfect if you know the local traffic that follows - Gallarate exit: further away, but you stay on the main road longer
### Timing and impact on schedules
The reopening of the exit is scheduled for 5 AM on Thursday, September 10th. This means that those leaving home in the morning (between 5:30 AM and 6:30 AM) will find the interchange already in operation, without the need to resort to alternative routes. Conversely, the criticality focuses on the previous evening's return and very early departures (before 5 AM).
For a cross-border commuter who normally returns from work between 6 PM and 10 PM, the critical window is real: the closure starts at 10 PM, so those leaving Varesotto at 9:30 PM-9:45 PM may find traffic converging towards alternative exits while they themselves approach the closure point.
### Staying informed
Autostrade provides real-time updates on traffic. If you have an urgent transit need on the night of September 9th (overtime work, emergency), it is advisable to check the status of the highway directly on the official Autostrade channels or on the most updated navigation applications a few minutes before departure.
For those who do not have specific urgencies that night, the simplest solution remains: postpone the return to after 5 AM on Thursday morning, when traffic returns to normal. This way, you completely avoid the inconvenience.
### Tools to optimize the trip
Use [the paycheck calculator](nav:calculator) to check your work rhythms and not take risks with driving times. If your daily commute is particularly stressful, it might be worth a conversation with your employer about possible temporary adjustments to the schedule for that evening. Many employers in Varesotto are sensitive to the logistical needs of their cross-border workers.

item.title: Living in Arosio, working in Ticino: border guide
item.description: From geographical location to tax advantages: everything that those who want to move to Arosio and work in the Canton of Ticino need to know about the rights of the border worker.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Arosio is on the border with Ticino: ideal location for commuters working in Switzerland - From January 1, 2024, the New Cross-Border Agreement introduces allowances of CHF 10,000 (new commuters) - Withholding tax is deducted in Switzerland; Italy avoids double taxation through tax credit - AVS/AI/IPG contributions: 5.3% borne by the employee, managed by the Ticino employer
## Key facts - **What**: Residence in Italy (Como province), work in Canton Ticino with permit G - When: Regime active from January 1, 2024 for all new commuters - Where: Arosio (Como, Italy) — border crossings to Ticino (Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo) - Who: Commuters with permit G, administered by Swiss SEM and Italian Revenue Agency - Allowance amount: CHF 10,000 annually (new commuters); CHF 7,500 (previous commuters, transitional regime 2024–2033) - Withholding tax rate: Set by federal regulations and cantonal tax administrations
### Arosio: a logical choice for commuters Arosio is a municipality in the province of Como, located a few kilometers from the Swiss border. Its proximity to the crossings connecting Lombardy to Ticino (Chiasso, Brogeda, Gaggiolo) makes it a convenient residential base for those working in major Ticino centers: Lugano, Mendrisio, Bellinzona, Locarno. The cost of living in the Como area is generally lower compared to the Canton of Ticino, a non-secondary element for commuters who receive Swiss salaries but support part of their personal life in Italy. The local community offers healthcare, educational, and administrative services, with the Como Revenue Agency available for Italian tax issues. The geographical proximity reduces commuting times, a crucial factor for those who face border crossings daily. For a commuter, choosing to reside in Arosio means balancing access to the Ticino job market with the economic sustainability of Italian residence. ### The tax regime of the cross-border worker: how it works
Anyone residing in Arosio and working in Ticino is subject to the G permit (cross-border), which allows daily or weekly commuting. From a tax perspective, the withholding tax (deducted by the Swiss employer) is paid exclusively in Switzerland — never in both countries. This is a fundamental principle: the income from dependent work of a cross-border worker is never taxed twice. Italy, through the Italo-Swiss Bilateral Convention signed on December 9, 1976, grants a tax credit (section CE of the 730 declaration) that compensates for the tax already paid in Switzerland. Switzerland is not a member of the EU, so taxation follows specific regimes, not the ordinary European system. The Italian tax credit is the key tool to avoid double taxation.
### Allowances and new 2024 agreement
The New Cross-Border Agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, and effective from January 1, 2024, has redefined the tax allowances. For new cross-border workers (those not yet registered as such before July 17, 2023), the allowance is CHF 10,000 annually: incomes up to this threshold do not generate income tax in Ticino. Cross-border workers already active before July 17, 2023, benefit from a transitional regime: an allowance of CHF 7,500 from 2024 to 2033, with gradual increases up to CHF 10,000. This distinction is important for correctly calculating the taxable base and planning the income declaration. The Italian Revenue Agency recognizes the tax credit in section CE, reducing or zeroing the gross Italian IRPEF according to the ordinary rates: 23% up to 28,000 euros, 35% up to 50,000, 43% over 50,000.
### Pension contributions: AVS, LPP, and health insurance
Cross-border workers pay Swiss social security contributions: AVS (Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance) and AI (Disability Insurance) at a rate of 5.3% of the gross salary at the employee's expense, plus an equivalent employer contribution. The IPG (Loss of Earnings Allowance) contribution of 0.3% is added. Unemployment insurance (AD) and accident insurance (LAINF) follow federal rates: respectively 1.1% up to CHF 148,200 annual salary and 0.7-1.5%. The LPP (occupational pension, second pillar) varies by age group: from 7% to 18% depending on the pension fund and professional category. In Italy, the equivalent is managed by INPS (National Institute for Social Security), but a cross-border worker working in Switzerland pays exclusively Swiss contributions: they do not pay simultaneously in both systems. Health insurance (LAMal) is mandatory in Switzerland; cross-border workers with a G permit have the right to choose and can insure themselves with a Swiss institution or maintain Italian coverage (with verification of regulatory compatibility). The deductibles for adults in LAMal range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Practical procedure: what to do before moving
#### 1. Request the G permit
Before moving to Arosio, the Ticino employer must submit a request for authorization to hire to the SEM (Swiss State Secretariat for Migration) and the competent cantonal authorities. The G permit is nominative (linked to the employer) and has a maximum validity of 5 years, renewable. The documentation requires: signed employment contract, curriculum vitae, Swiss employer identification, proof of minimum income (determined at the cantonal level). It is advisable to verify the specific details with the Como Prefecture (Italian side) and the Department of Finance and Economy of the Canton Ticino (Swiss side).
#### 2. Open a bank account and Italian tax formalities
On the Italian side, it is necessary to register with the competent Agenzia Entrate for the province of Como (office of Arosio or district) and obtain or update the tax code. Those who work in Switzerland must inform the Municipality of Arosio that they are cross-border workers: this communication facilitates the recognition of status with the local public administration. A bank account with an Italian bank in Como or Switzerland is essential: many Ticino employers pay salaries via SEPA bank transfer, so it is useful to have an Italian or Swiss IBAN. Some cross-border workers open accounts with banks operating in Switzerland, simplifying administrative management.
#### 3. Income declaration and CE section
Every year (by June 30 for the ordinary declaration), those who work in Ticino must submit the 730 model to the Agenzia Entrate of the province of Como. In the 730 model, the **CE section** is specific for cross-border workers: here, the tax already paid in Switzerland (withheld by the employer) is declared and the tax credit is quantified. The Agenzia Entrate compares the Italian tax due (gross IRPEF according to ordinary rates) with the recognized credit and determines the refund, the integration, or the balance due. It is advisable to use a tax accountant specialized in cross-border taxation to ensure the correct compilation of the CE section and maximize the credit.
#### 4. Key contacts and resources
For Swiss tax issues: Canton Ticino, Division of Contributions (federal section); for work permit: SEM (Canton Ticino section). For Italian aspects: Agenzia Entrate Como (district office), Municipality of Arosio (secretariat/registry), Como Prefecture (general administrative issues). A net salary calculator is available on our website to estimate the impact of taxes and contributions on the Swiss paycheck before the decision to move.
#### Critical deadlines
- G permit request: To be submitted before the official start date of work (usually 2-4 weeks in advance) - Agenzia Entrate registration: Within 30 days of starting Italian residence - 730 declaration: By June 30 of the year following the income received - AVS contribution payment: Monthly or on the schedule indicated by the employer (usually at the end of the month)
Moving to Arosio as a cross-border worker is administratively feasible if planned in advance. The interaction between Swiss and Italian rules requires attention to detail and respect for deadlines. To avoid surprises from the paycheck or tax declaration, use our net salary calculator and verify in advance the impact of Swiss-Italian taxation on your income. Then, contact the competent administrations or a specialized consultant to further refine the contractual and pension details.

item.title: Milan: Niguarda and Istituto Tumori join forces for oncological emergencies
item.description: The Niguarda Hospital and the IRCCS Fondazione Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori in Milan have signed an operational protocol to ensure continuity of care for cancer patients in case of emergencies.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Operational protocol between Niguarda Hospital and the National Cancer Institute of Milan - Objective: to avoid interruptions in the care pathway of cancer patients - Coordination by ATS Milan and the University of Milan
## Key facts - **What**: Operational protocol between Niguarda Hospital and the National Cancer Institute - When: Not specified - Where: Milan - Who: Niguarda Hospital, National Cancer Institute, ATS Milan, University of Milan - Amount: Not specified
Niguarda Hospital and the Fondazione IRCCS National Cancer Institute (INT) of Milan have signed an operational protocol to ensure continuity of care for cancer patients in case of emergencies. The protocol, coordinated by ATS of the Metropolitan City of Milan and the School of Medical Oncology of the University of Milan, aims to avoid interruptions in the care pathway of patients. The National Cancer Institute, a reference center for cancer care and research, does not have its own Emergency Department, so patients who face an emergency may need to access another hospital facility.
### Protocol Objective The protocol aims to ensure that the transition from one institution to another occurs without interrupting the continuity of care, by putting the emergency department of Niguarda in direct communication with the specialists of the INT. When a patient being treated at the National Cancer Institute arrives at the Niguarda Emergency Department, emergency professionals can promptly coordinate with the oncologists of the INT, sharing clinical information, ongoing therapies, and care priorities. The goal is to allow Niguarda doctors to intervene while considering the oncological pathway already undertaken by the patient.
The primary objective remains to stabilize the person and address the emergency, but the connection between the teams also serves to avoid inappropriate interventions and, when conditions allow, to facilitate the patient's return to their reference oncology center. According to the protocol, in most cases, the resumption of care by the National Cancer Institute occurs within 24-48 hours of the Emergency Department notification.
Even when immediate transfer is not possible, the exchange between specialists allows for continuity in clinical decisions and therapy management. The project fits into the model of clinical-assistance networks promoted by the Lombardy Region, with the aim of strengthening collaboration between facilities and professionals and reducing the fragmentation of care pathways.
In this case, the Lombardy Oncological Network and the emergency-urgency system are connected, creating a structured link between a reference oncology institute and a large Emergency Department. ### Implications for Cross-Border Workers The operational protocol between Niguarda Hospital and the National Cancer Institute of Milan has important implications for cross-border workers who work in Lombardy and reside in Ticino. This agreement ensures that cross-border cancer patients can receive continuous and coordinated care in case of emergencies, avoiding interruptions in their treatment path.
### Procedure for Cross-Border Patients When a cross-border patient undergoing treatment at the National Cancer Institute arrives at the Niguarda Emergency Department, emergency professionals can promptly coordinate with the oncologists at the INT, sharing clinical information, ongoing therapies, and care priorities. This allows Niguarda doctors to intervene while considering the oncological path already undertaken by the patient.
### Possible Scenarios A cross-border worker in a similar situation could benefit from this protocol, ensuring that their therapies are not interrupted and that they continue to receive appropriate care. The protocol provides that in most cases, the resumption of care by the National Cancer Institute will occur within 24-48 hours of the Emergency Department notification.
### Actions for Cross-Border Workers Cross-border workers facing a medical emergency can rely on this protocol to ensure the continuity of their care. It is important that patients and their families are informed about this procedure and that they promptly turn to the Niguarda Emergency Department in case of emergency.
### Deadlines and Procedure The operational protocol is already in effect, and patients can immediately benefit from this collaboration between the two facilities. There are no specific deadlines to be met, but it is crucial that patients follow the doctors' instructions and present themselves at the Niguarda Emergency Department if needed.
### Useful Tools For further information on the services offered by Niguarda Hospital and the National Cancer Institute, cross-border workers can consult the websites of the two institutions. Additionally, the [tax calculator](nav:calculator) can be used to obtain detailed information about their tax and insurance situation.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### Conclusion The operational protocol between Niguarda Hospital and the National Cancer Institute of Milan represents an important step forward in the management of emergencies for oncological patients, ensuring continuity of care and improving collaboration between healthcare facilities. Cross-border workers who work in Lombardy and reside in Ticino can benefit from this initiative, which ensures them coordinated and timely assistance in case of need.
### Actions to Take Cross-border workers who find themselves facing a medical emergency should promptly turn to the Niguarda Emergency Room, where emergency professionals can coordinate with the oncologists of the National Cancer Institute to ensure continuity of care. It is important that patients and their families are informed about this procedure and follow the doctors' instructions.
### Useful Tools For further information on the services offered by Niguarda Hospital and the National Cancer Institute, cross-border workers can consult the websites of the two institutions. Additionally, you can use the [tax calculator](nav:calculator) to obtain detailed information about your tax and insurance situation.
### Final CTA To deepen your tax and insurance situation, use our [tax calculator](nav:calculator). This tool will allow you to obtain detailed and personalized information about your situation, helping you to make informed decisions and plan your future effectively.

item.title: Living in Griante and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Benefits, procedures, costs and regulations for those who choose to live in Griante working in the Canton of Ticino as a border worker
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New cross-border agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - Withholding tax deducted exclusively in Switzerland - AVS and LPP mandatory for employees in Switzerland - Permit G required from SEM for Italian cross-border workers
## Key facts - **What**: Cross-border worker G (employee in Switzerland, resident in Italy) - When: New agreement in force from 1 January 2024 - Where: Griante (Como), working in Canton Ticino - Who: Cross-border workers according to the Italy-Switzerland bilateral agreement - Tax: Deducted exclusively in Switzerland, no double taxation - LAMal: Right to choose Swiss health insurance - AVS/LPP: Mandatory contributions (5.3% + 7-18% depending on age)
Living in Griante and working in Canton Ticino as a cross-border worker is a common choice for those seeking a balance between living space, quality of life, and job opportunities. From 1 January 2024, with the new cross-border agreement (Law 83 of 13 June 2023, signed on 23 December 2020), the rules for taxation and social security are clearly defined and ensure legal clarity.
The cross-border worker "G" is legally defined as a person residing abroad who works in Switzerland, commuting daily or at least once a week. For Italians, the tax regime is particularly advantageous: the withholding tax on employment income is deducted exclusively by Switzerland, not by Italy. The convention against double taxation of 9 December 1976 guarantees this mechanism; in the Italian declaration (CE section of the 730 form), a tax credit is applied for the amount already paid in Switzerland.
### Social security contributions and pay structure
Those working in Switzerland must contribute to various social security schemes: AVS (first pillar) at 5.3% for the employee, plus an additional 5.3% from the employer; AI (disability insurance) and IPG (maternity allowance) included in the 5.3%; LPP (second pillar, company pension fund) from 7% to 18% depending on age, starting at 25 years; AD and AC (unemployment and insolvency) at 1.1% with a cap at CHF 148.200; LAINF (occupational accidents) between 0.7% and 1.5%. These contributions are managed at the federal level by the AFC (Federal Tax Administration). The AVS contributions paid in Switzerland are recognized by the Italian INPS for the right to the Italian pension.
### Health insurance and LAMal
As a cross-border worker, you have the option to choose health insurance: you can maintain Italian coverage or join a Swiss health insurance (LAMal). The adult deductibles in LAMal range from CHF 300 to CHF 2.500 depending on the chosen insurance. Many cross-border workers opt for LAMal due to the geographical proximity to their workplace in Ticino.
### The Permit G
The residence permit for cross-border workers requires an application to the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) with the original employment contract, a valid passport, and proof of residence in Griante. The permit is linked to the duration of the employment contract and requires annual renewal as long as the contract continues. Moving to Griante as a border worker involves significant administrative adjustments in the management of the payroll, tax return and insurance coverage. Net income changes significantly compared to a scenario of residency in Ticino or Italy with Italian work, since the structure of withholdings is radically different.
### The structure of withholdings and declaration
Withholdings for AVS/AI/IPG (5.3%), AD/AC (1.1%), LPP (7-18%) and LAINF (0.7-1.5%) will appear in the Swiss paycheck of a border crossing. The cantonal source tax varies according to salary bracket and personal circumstances; it is calculated by the cantonal tax administrations and paid independently to the Swiss tax authorities by the employer.
In the Italian declaration, the income from foreign work must be indicated in the EC framework of form 730. The Swiss tax paid generates a tax credit that reduces or eliminates the Italian IRPEF (23% up to EUR 28,000, 35% between EUR 28,001 and EUR 50,000, 43% over EUR 50,000). For old frontier workers (before 17 July 2023) there is an exemption of CHF 7,500 on a transitional basis until 2033; new frontier workers benefit from an exemption of CHF 10,000. This structural mechanism avoids double taxation and represents the main tax advantage of the border regime compared to other residence options.

Before moving to Griante, follow an ordered checklist to avoid administrative delays and tax surprises. The process is not complex, but it requires 2-4 months in advance to complete all steps and obtain the G permit. ### Pre-move timeline and checklist **2-4 months before**: Inform your employer of your intention to move to Griante and verify that the contract allows the frontier regime. Contact the SEM for guidance on the G permit procedure. 1-2 months before: Prepare complete documentation (valid passport, original or certified copy of employment contract, proof of temporary residence in Griante). If you opt for LAMal, contact the Ticino health insurance funds and request a proposal. 2-4 weeks before: Submit the G permit application to the SEM with all documentation. Sign the rental contract or purchase agreement in Griante to obtain proof of permanent residence. Upon moving: Update your address with the local registry office in Griante. Notify your employer of the new address for updating the payroll system and personal data. Within 30 days of moving: Send the change of residence notification to the Italian Tax Agency. ### Essential documents - Valid passport or ID card (with at least 6 months remaining validity) - Swiss employment contract (original or certified copy) - Proof of residence in Griante (registered rental contract, notarial purchase agreement, or letter from the local authority) - SEM forms for the G permit application (available at www.sem.admin.ch) - Last three pay slips (to verify taxable income) - Banking documentation (IBAN, account references, useful for INPS and Tax Agency checks) - Change of residence declaration to the Tax Agency (form available at www.agenziaentrate.gov.it) ### Contacts and resources SEM (State Secretariat for Migration): G permit application and renewal — www.sem.admin.ch Italian Tax Agency: change of residence notification — www.agenziaentrate.gov.it Ticino Migration Office: local checks and administrative procedures Employer: updating personal data, frontier payroll configuration Moving to Griante is manageable with order and timeliness. item.title: Living in Bellagio, working in Ticino: border guide
item.description: Moving to Bellagio and working in Ticino as a border worker: discover the tax regime, AVS contributions, LAMal and how to plan the transfer.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- Withholding tax only deducted in Switzerland for cross-border workers - New Cross-Border Agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - AVS/AI contributions: 5.3% for employees, LAINF 0.7–1.5% - LAMal: deductible CHF 300–2500, option right Permit G
## Key facts
- **Withholding tax**: Deducted only in Switzerland - New Agreement: Effective from 1 January 2024 - AVS/AI: 5.3% for employees - LAINF: 0.7–1.5% depending on sector - LPP: 7–18% by age group (from 25 years) - Deductible: €7,500 for old cross-border workers (until 2033), €10,000 for new ones
Bellagio, overlooking Lake Como, is a popular residential choice for those working in Ticino. The province of Como is within manageable distances from major Ticino work centers: Lugano, Mendrisio, Chiasso, Bellinzona. For this move, understanding the tax, contribution, and insurance regime governing Swiss-Italian cross-border workers is essential, especially after the New Cross-Border Agreement came into effect on 1 January 2024.
The tax system is the central pillar. The withholding tax on employment income is deducted solely by Switzerland, avoiding double taxation. Italy subsequently applies the tax credit (CE box of the 730 tax return) to recognize what has been paid to the Swiss tax authorities. This mechanism, regulated by the Convention on Double Taxation between Italy and Switzerland signed on 9 December 1976, protects the cross-border worker from excessive tax pressure.
### The tax regime: old and new cross-border workers
The New Agreement introduces a significant distinction. Old cross-border workers (those already in this status before 17 July 2023) enjoy an annual exemption of €7,500 until 2033, under a transitional regime. New cross-border workers benefit from an annual deductible of €10,000. This difference is central to the calculation of taxable income in Italy.
Swiss social security contributions are deducted directly by the Ticino company from the gross salary. The AVS/AI/IPG rate is fixed at 5.3% for employees, while the employer contributes the same amount. The accident insurance (LAINF) varies between 0.7% and 1.5%, depending on the sector. The professional pension fund (LPP) requires contributions between 7% and 18%, depending on the age group (from 25 years onwards).
The cantonal and communal tax in Ticino is added according to federal and cantonal rates, administered by the Swiss authorities. You can [calculate your net income using our tax calculator](nav:calculator) to verify exactly how much you will earn after deductions. ## What to Consider Before Moving to Bellagio
Moving to Bellagio to work in Ticino involves significant practical and financial considerations. The cost of living is the first evaluation: Bellagio is an expensive residential area on Lake Como. Rents and property prices reflect the scenic value and proximity to the Swiss border. A commuter must assess whether the net salary in Ticino (after AVS deductions of 5.3% and LAINF 0.7–1.5%) compensates for housing and commuting costs. A comparative table between monthly net income and rental costs is essential for making an informed decision.
### Advantages and Disadvantages of the Choice
The advantages of living in Bellagio include quality of life, a lakeside landscape, an established community of commuters (offering support networks and practical knowledge), and geographical proximity to Ticino, ideal for daily commuting. The disadvantages include significant rental and property costs, daily commuting on mountain roads exposed to weather variability, and the obligation to subscribe to health insurance.
Regarding the choice of insurance: commuters with Permit G have the option to choose between Swiss LAMal and Italian SSN. If you opt for LAMal, the deductibles for adults range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 annually, depending on the coverage. If you remain in the Italian SSN, you must notify the Swiss authorities of your renunciation of LAMal. This choice directly impacts health coverage and annual costs.
### Registration Procedure and Permit G
Before moving, ensure you have the [Permit G (commuters)](nav:permits). This is mandatory for daily work in Switzerland. The documentation is submitted by the Ticino employer, who coordinates with the Swiss authorities (SEM — State Secretariat for Migration). Without Permit G, the move is legally prohibited.
A commuter should also consider: the distance to the nearest border crossings (Brogeda, Gaggiolo, Ponte Tresa, Chiasso) closest to the workplace, the stability of the Ticino job (commuting jobs are more affected by economic conditions), and the effect of currency (salary in CHF, expenses in EUR, with exchange rate fluctuations impacting purchasing power).
### Opportunity Cost Calculation
Before any move, subtract fixed costs from the gross monthly amount: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3%, LAINF 0.7–1.5%, LPP 7–18%, federal and cantonal Ticino withholding tax. Compare the resulting net amount with rents, utilities, commuting costs (fuel, maintenance, or public transport subscriptions), and living expenses in Bellagio. If the margin is positive and sustainable over time, the move is economically justified.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Checklist for moving and starting as a cross-border commuter
Step 1: Calculate your net monthly income
Before any move, estimate your net income using a [cross-border tax calculator](nav:calculator). Subtract from the gross amount: - AVS/AI/IPG: 5.3% - LAINF: between 0.7% and 1.5% (depends on the sector) - LPP: between 7% and 18% (depends on age, from 25 onwards) - Federal and cantonal Ticino withholding tax
The result is your net monthly income, to be compared with the actual cost of rent, utilities, and living in Bellagio.
Step 2: Verify the G Permit with your employer
Ensure you obtain the G Permit before moving. The Ticino employer submits the documentation to the Swiss authorities (SEM). This permit is mandatory for daily work in Switzerland and is not a formality you can handle independently: your employer coordinates the process.
Step 3: Choose health insurance (LAMal or Italian SSN)
With the G Permit, you have the option to: - Join the Swiss LAMal (deductible CHF 300–2.500 for adults, depending on the chosen coverage) - Stay in the Italian SSN (with official notification to the Swiss authorities)
The choice affects premiums/deductibles and coverage. Consult a LAMal agent or local health authorities to evaluate which solution is best.
Step 4: Italian tax registration and communication to the Revenue Agency
Notify the Italian Revenue Agency of the change of residence. Your income will be subject to the new cross-border regime: - If you are an old cross-border commuter (already such before July 17, 2023): exemption €7.500 annually until 2033 - If you are a new cross-border commuter: exemption €10.000 annually
These exemptions reduce the Italian taxable income and result in lower tax payments.
Step 5: Swiss bank account and currency management
Many cross-border commuters maintain accounts in both countries to manage CHF (salary) and EUR (expenses). Open an account with a Ticino bank. Check exchange fees and management costs: some institutions offer cross-border accounts with advantageous conditions.
Step 6: Calculate the total cost of commuting and decide on the means
Estimate fuel (if private car), travel (if train/bus), vehicle maintenance, Swiss vignette if necessary. Some cross-border commuters choose public transport (Trenitalia + Swiss railways) to avoid the costs and stress of daily driving. Compare all options with the gross salary advantage: if the commuting cost is too high, the move might not be convenient.

item.title: Figino Serenza: guide for border workers in Ticino
item.description: Permit G, taxation, LAMal and costs: everything that changes if you live in Figino Serenza and work in the Canton of Ticino as a border worker.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - Permit G mandatory to work in Ticino from Lombardy - Withholding tax only in Switzerland, no double taxation - LAMal mandatory in Switzerland with CHF 300–2500 deductibles - AVS/LPP: contributions 5.3% on salary + employer payments
## Key facts - **What**: Permit G + taxation for cross-border workers - When: From January 1, 2024 (new agreement in force) - Where: Cross-border workers Italy-Ticino from Lombardy - Who: SEM, SECO, Tax Agency, INPS - Tax rate: Single in Switzerland, tax credit in Italy - LAMal deductible: CHF 300–2500 annual for adults - Tax exemption threshold: €7,500 (historic from 17/7/2023), €10,000 (new cross-border workers)
Those who choose to live in Figino Serenza and work in the Canton of Ticino have access to an increasingly common opportunity among cross-border workers: staying in Lombardy, maintaining Italian residency, but transferring the Swiss salary. However, this model involves precise rules for taxation, social security, and insurance. The Permit G (authorization from the SEM) is the first mandatory document.
### Permit G and Tax Treatment
The Permit G allows Italian residents to work legally in Switzerland. Those living in Figino Serenza must apply for it at the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) at least 6–8 weeks before the start date of work. Required documents: signed job offer, passport or ID card, residence certificate from the Italian municipality, proof of LAMal subscription.
A key point: the withholding tax is deducted exclusively in Switzerland. There is no double taxation CHF-EUR. The Convention between Italy and Switzerland of December 9, 1976 regulates this matter. Italy does not tax income from work carried out in Switzerland for cross-border workers; rather, they declare the income in the Italian model 730 and apply the tax credit (CE section) to avoid overlaps.
The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement, signed on December 23, 2020 and entered into force on January 1, 2024 (Law 83 of June 13, 2023 in Italy), introduces tax-free thresholds: historic cross-border workers (those already such before July 17, 2023) enjoy an exemption up to €7,500 annually in a transitional regime until 2033; new cross-border workers have a threshold of €10,000.
### LAMal and Social Security
Swiss health insurance (LAMal) is mandatory for all workers. The cross-border worker must subscribe to it within 3 months of the start of the employment relationship. Deductibles for adults range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 annually, depending on the policy and chosen fund. The employer typically covers a portion of the premium according to the collective agreement.
On the social security front, AVS/AI/IPG contributions (employee part) are 5.3% of gross salary. The company pays the same 5.3%. For unemployment (AD/AC), the rate is 1.1% with a cap of CHF 148,200 on annual salary. Accident insurance (LAINF) varies between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector. The second pillar (LPP, supplementary pension) involves contributions between 7% and 18% depending on age, from the 25th year of age. Living in Lombardy, Working in Switzerland: The Economic Calculation
One of the main advantages of living in Figino Serenza and working in Ticino is the cost of living differential. Housing, food, and services in Lombardy are generally lower than in Ticino. This allows for a significant monthly savings potential. However, the commuter must balance this benefit with the recurring costs of commuting: fuel, highway A2 (for which the annual Swiss vignette CHF 40 is required), parking at the Ticino workplace, possible tolls.
The salary is paid in CHF (Swiss francs), while housing, food, and local expenses in Figino Serenza are in EUR (euros). The margin of convenience depends on a careful evaluation of individual items: rent, utilities, food, transportation, healthcare services. Many commuters use [specialized salary calculators](nav:calculator) to simulate the actual net income and compare it with the cost of living.
### Border Crossings and Commuter Routes
From Figino Serenza, the commuter has access to multiple border crossings into Ticino. **Chiasso** (via highway A2) is the most direct route to southern Ticino (Lugano, Mendrisio, south of Lugano border). Brogeda is a less congested alternative during peak hours. Gaggiolo is suitable for those working in the northern lake area (Luino, areas near Ticino). Ponte Tresa serves western Sopraceneri (Locarno, Ascona, Bellinzona).
Wait times at the border vary depending on the time of day and seasonal congestion. During morning and evening peak hours, Chiasso can experience delays. Some commuters adjust their departure times or use public transportation: Como–Chiasso regional trains, then Swiss rail connection to the destination (Lugano, Bellinzona, Locarno).
Consulting [border crossing and historical traffic information](nav:traffic-history) before planning the route is a common practice.
### Administrative Issues Before Moving
Before moving from Figino Serenza to Ticino, specific bureaucratic steps must be completed:
- Notify the Figino Serenza municipality of the change of residence and obtain the residence certificate - Inform the Italian Revenue Agency of the new address and Swiss income source - Apply for a G permit with the competent SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) - Sign a LAMal contract with a Swiss insurance company (CSS, Helsana, Visana, SWICA, etc.) - Notify the Ticino company of the new address and start date - Consider opening a Swiss bank account for salary receipt (including CHF-EUR exchange fees in the evaluation) - In the first year, consult a tax advisor for correct income tax filing (CE box for tax credit)
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-Step: Transfer and First Deadlines
Step 1 — Job Search and Written Offer. Identify the Ticino company and obtain a signed and dated job offer. This document is mandatory for the G Permit application.
Step 2 — G Permit Application. Contact the competent SEM (for Ticino: SEM Bellinzona) at least 6–8 weeks before the start date. Required: passport/identity card, job offer, Italian residence certificate, proof of LAMal subscription (even provisional).
Step 3 — Change Italian Residence. Go to the Figino Serenza Town Hall and register the transfer. Obtain the residence certificate for the G Permit application and for communications with the Tax Agency.
**Step 4 — LAMal Subscription.** Contact a Swiss insurer directly and activate the coverage. Major insurance companies operate online. Note: It is mandatory within 3 months from the start of work, but it is advisable to activate it earlier for the G Permit.
Step 5 — Bank Account. Consider opening a Swiss account with UBS, Credit Suisse, Raiffeisen, or others, or receiving the salary on an Italian account with subsequent CHF-EUR exchange. Evaluate fees and spreads.
Step 6 — First Year Tax Declaration. Consult a tax advisor for the Italian 730 form. Indicate the income declared in Switzerland and the tax credit in the CE section to avoid double taxation.
### Recurring Costs to Budget
Once transferred to Figino Serenza, the cross-border worker incurs:
- Rent/mortgage: Variable depending on the area and square meters in Figino Serenza - Highway and fuel: Estimated travel (e.g., 25 km × days/week × 52 weeks), considering gasoline and vignette CHF 40/year - LAMal: CHF 300–500 monthly depending on the deductible and policy - Bank Account: If Swiss, check monthly or annual fees (some accounts offer free management if the salary is domiciled) - Currency Exchange: If salary transfer in CHF → Italian account in EUR, consider bank spreads (0.5–2% depending on the bank) - Public Transport: Possible LC (Lugano–Como) or regional train subscription if choosing a combination of car/train
### Available Tools
To simulate your net paycheck considering taxation, AVS, LAMal, and other cross-border contributions, consult [the specialized salary calculator](nav:calculator). You can enter the Swiss gross and see the actual net.
If you want to compare the cost of living in Ticino vs. bordering Lombardy (rents, goods, services), try [the cost of living comparator](nav:cost-of-living). This will help you evaluate the real savings by living in Figino Serenza.
For managing recurring CHF-EUR exchange (e.g., monthly transfers to Italian accounts), the exchange rate tool shows the best current banking conditions.
Finally, receive monthly updates on cross-border regulations, tax deadlines, and job opportunities in Ticino by subscribing to the Frontaliere Ticino newsletter — access from the [calculator section](nav:calculator).

item.description: The Municipality of Como has opened preferential lanes and ZTL zones for vehicles to Switzerland. Here are the authorized routes and how to move around the construction site.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - Construction site on Como Lakefront: underground services being redone; priority lanes and ZTL open - Vehicles heading to Switzerland can use via Rodari–piazza Roma–piazza Cavour–via Cairoli - Disruptions on the Lariana (Como-Bellagio); nine mayors have protested
## Key facts - **What**: Opening of priority lanes (via Sauro, Battisti, Milano) + ZTL passable for vehicles heading to Switzerland - When: For two days; end not yet specified - Where: Como, Lakefront; Lariana road Como-Bellagio - Who: Municipality of Como, mayors of the East shore of the lake, Acus - ZTL route: via Rodari–piazza Roma–via Bianchi Giovini–piazza Cavour–via Fontana–via Cairoli
### The construction site that paralyzes the passage to Switzerland The construction site started two days ago on the Como Lakefront for the renovation of underground services is causing devastating disruptions to normal traffic. The hole that opened months earlier made a deep structural intervention necessary, but the impact on traffic has been more severe than expected. The Lariana, the road connecting Como to Bellagio and one of the main traffic corridors to Ticino and the Chiasso border, is practically blocked. Italian cross-border workers who normally work in the Canton of Ticino usually travel this road to reach the border crossings. With the ongoing construction, the flow has completely jammed. The situation was so serious that nine mayors of the East shore of the lake sent a furious protest to the Municipality of Como and had even contacted the prefect to request intervention. Acus also reported the problem.
### The three priority lanes opened by the Municipality Faced with growing pressure, the Municipality of Como announced a series of temporary derogations from the normal traffic discipline, starting with the priority lanes. Until the completion of the lakefront works, the following priority lanes have been opened and made passable: - Via Sauro - Via Battisti - Via Milano, towards Milan Normally, priority lanes are reserved for buses, taxis, and vehicles with special permits. Opening them to ordinary vehicles represents a structured derogation, not an informal exception. This measure aims to increase the capacity of the road network in critical directions and to channel the flow through routes parallel to the blocked Lariana.
### Opening of the ZTL for traffic heading to Switzerland The most relevant measure for cross-border workers is the opening of a corridor through the Limited Traffic Zone (ZTL) of Como. Normally, the ZTL is closed to unauthorized vehicles, but during the construction phase, the Municipality has authorized passage for those heading to Switzerland, provided they follow a specific route: Via Rodari → Piazza Roma → Via Bianchi Giovini → Piazza Cavour → Via Fontana → Via Cairoli This route allows vehicles heading to the Swiss border crossings to cross Como without incurring penalties for violating the ZTL. The stated goal is to "ensure, compatibly with the necessary and unavoidable construction site, the greatest possible fluidity of traffic and contain the disruptions." The measures remain in effect until the completion of the works, the end of which has not yet been officially specified. ## Real impact on the cross-border commuter: times and routes
For the cross-border commuter who lives in Como or in the surrounding municipalities and works in Ticino, the construction site is not just local news. It is a concrete loss of time and potentially measurable in terms of hourly earnings. Those who normally take 15-20 minutes to travel the Lariana towards Chiasso now find themselves having to follow alternative routes that require precise navigation and add distance.
The choice between the priority lanes and the ZTL route is not intuitive. The priority lanes on via Sauro, Battisti, and Milano towards Milano can be useful for those coming from the north of the city, but for those living in central Como or in the lakeside municipalities and wanting to reach Chiasso, the added value is uncertain. The Lariana was the direct route; the alternatives revolve around the urban center, adding at least 5-10 minutes.
### How to navigate the ZTL route: dangers and procedures
The route via Rodari–piazza Roma–via Bianchi Giovini–piazza Cavour–via Fontana–via Cairoli is not the natural path. It requires knowing Como, following specific turns, and being careful not to exit the authorized route, risking a fine for violating the ZTL.
Many cross-border commuters do not know Como in detail and, relying on the navigator, might receive alternative suggestions that exit the authorized zone. In this case, a fine of several hundred euros could result from not respecting the ZTL exemption.
**Concrete actions**: Save the route on the navigator BEFORE having to travel it. Test the route during low traffic times (e.g., on the weekend) to familiarize yourself with the turns. Check on Google Maps or Apple Maps the real-time duration during peak hours compared to the departure with the Lariana free.
### Public transport as a structural alternative
If the construction site lasts more than two weeks, many cross-border commuters choose to abandon the car for the train. Como is served by two main stations (Como Lago and Como San Giovanni) with direct connections to Ticino via the regional Tilo trains. The journey Como–Chiasso–Lugano is covered by regular and reliable schedules, without traffic stress.
The cost of a weekly or monthly train subscription might be higher than fuel, but during the construction site, it represents an investment in punctuality. A cross-border commuter who takes 45 minutes instead of 20 is losing 25 minutes a day = 2 hours a week = 8 hours a month. If the gross hourly wage is higher than CHF 25, the cost of the delay exceeds CHF 200 monthly, making the train subscription economically convenient.
### When does the construction site end? A missing detail
The source does not specify when the Municipality of Como plans to complete the work. This is a critical element for the cross-border commuter: if the construction site lasts a week, it is worth adapting temporarily; if it lasts months, it is necessary to consider structural solutions (partial teleworking, flexible hours, permanent public transport). The Municipality should clearly communicate this date, but for the moment, it remains uncertain.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Practical procedure: what to do immediately
If you are a commuter leaving Como for Ticino during the construction period, follow this checklist:
1. Check the status of the construction site Contact the Municipality of Como or its official website to confirm if the construction site is still active and when it is expected to be completed. Do not rely solely on general news; call the Municipality's single number for up-to-date information.
2. Save the ZTL route on your navigator If you decide to use the route through the ZTL (via Rodari–piazza Roma–via Bianchi Giovini–piazza Cavour–via Fontana–via Cairoli), load it as a "saved route" on Google Maps or Apple Maps before you leave. This way, you will have step-by-step text and voice guidance.
3. Make a trial run during low traffic hours Drive the route once on the weekend or during peak hours to understand where the critical turns are, where the reference parking lots are, and what the actual travel time is.
**4. Compare total times** Calculate the total time from your home to the entrance of your employer in Ticino (or the Chiasso border crossing). Add: departure time + alternative route (e.g., ZTL with detours) + wait time at the border + arrival. If the delay is more than 30 minutes compared to the pre-construction situation, consider alternatives.
5. Consider telecommuting or flexible hours Contact your Swiss employer and explain the situation. Many cross-border contracts allow 1-2 days of telecommuting per week. Negotiating a partial week from home during the construction period may be more convenient than losing hours in traffic.
## Public transport: the savings calculator Trains Como–Chiasso–Lugano (operated by Tilo) guarantee fixed schedules and zero stress. The cost of a weekly pass is typically around CHF 60–80 for the Como–Chiasso zone. If your gross hourly wage is CHF 30 and you are losing 2 hours per week in traffic, the value of the lost time is CHF 60 per week, so the pass pays for itself.
[Consult the available public transport solutions to understand the schedules and costs of your route](nav:transport).
## The cost of delay in terms of salary A 30-minute daily delay corresponds to 2.5 hours lost per week. If your cross-border contract does not provide for weekly overtime recovery, you are effectively giving away time (and earnings). A useful tool is the [cross-border net salary calculator](nav:calculator): by entering your gross monthly salary and the number of hours lost per week in traffic, you can see how much the lost time is really worth in CHF and EUR.
If you find that the cost of the delay is higher than the alternative cost (e.g., rail pass, negotiated telecommuting), the economic choice is clear.
## Continuous monitoring of traffic at border crossings During the construction period, wait times at the Chiasso border crossing and other access points to Ticino may increase. [Regularly check the traffic history at the Ticino-Italy border crossings](nav:traffic-history) to understand if the bottleneck is shifting (e.g., from Como to the border) or if the Municipality's measures are actually working.
If the traffic at the border remains constant, it means that the alternative route in Como is working; if it increases, the problem has become systemic and it may be worth negotiating even more flexible hours with the employer or switching to a more permanent telecommuting solution for the construction period.

item.title: Center Assembly approves AVS financing with VAT
item.description: The Centre supports the financing of the 13th AVS annuity through a 0.4% VAT increase. Vote on 29 November. What changes for border workers?
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Centro Assembly approves AVS funding with 0.4% VAT increase - Swiss popular vote on 29 November - 164 votes in favor out of 183 delegates present
## Key facts - **What**: Centro Assembly supports funding of 13th AVS pension through VAT increase - When: 29 November (date of popular vote) - Where: Granges-Paccot, Canton of Fribourg - Who: 183 delegates of the Centro - Amount: VAT increase of 0.4 percentage points - Outcome: 164 votes in favor, 9 against, 10 abstentions
The Centro Assembly, meeting in Granges-Paccot in the Canton of Fribourg, expressed support for the additional funding of the AVS through an increase in the value-added tax (VAT). The vote recorded 164 votes in favor, 9 against, and 10 abstentions out of a total of 183 delegates. The proposed increase is 0.4 percentage points.
The decision concerns the funding of the 13th AVS pension, a measure that generates debates even within the party. Marie-France Roth Pasquier, a Fribourg national councillor, emphasized: "The 13th pension has been approved and must be funded." According to the politician, a rejection would not solve the structural problem of the pension system.
However, some delegates expressed significant concerns. They believe that the VAT-based model excessively penalizes the middle class. Furthermore, they argue that a different and more structural solution to the problem of Swiss pension funding is needed in the long term.
### The second item put to the vote
In addition to the AVS issue, the assembly unanimously approved the relaxation of restrictions on the export and re-export of military material. This revision has already been approved by the Federal Chambers. According to the Centro, a Switzerland capable of defending itself needs a solid industrial base and reliable international partnerships.
Both items will be put to the Swiss popular vote on 29 November. The 183 delegates present followed the party presidency's recommendations on both issues.
[Check your AVS situation](nav:pension) using the tools dedicated to cross-border commuters. ## What does this mean for cross-border commuters? For those who work in Switzerland and live in Italy, this decision has direct implications. The 0.4% increase in VAT affects the cost of living in Swiss territory, a relevant factor for cross-border commuters who travel daily across the border. However, the most significant aspect concerns the pension system itself.
### The AHV and mandatory contributions Cross-border commuters regularly pay AHV contributions on their Swiss paycheck. These contributions are mandatory and are withheld directly by the employer. Unlike some individual pension systems, the AHV operates on a solidarity basis: current workers finance today's retirees, with the expectation that tomorrow's workers will finance them.
The 13th AHV pension is an additional allowance paid once a year. For those with a limited pension income, this additional allowance can represent a significant contribution to the annual budget. Many cross-border retirees consider this amount part of their long-term financial planning.
### The impact of the VAT increase on daily expenses If the measure is approved in the vote on November 29, the 0.4% increase in VAT will be reflected in many goods and services purchased in Switzerland. For cross-border commuters, this is a matter of concrete budgeting: purchases of groceries in Ticino supermarkets, payment for services, medical services not covered by the LAMal, fuel — all will experience a slight increase.
Some representatives of the Center have suggested that other funding options could distribute the burden more fairly. Increases in mandatory contributions or revisions of federal tax rates could alternatively finance the system. However, the VAT method was preferred as it also affects foreign consumers, including tourists and daily cross-border commuters.
### The role of the November 29 vote [Discover how your AHV pension is calculated](nav:pension) with simulators dedicated to cross-border commuters. The popular vote on November 29 will be decisive. If the Swiss approve the AHV financing, the measure will come into effect according to the timetable set by the federal authorities. If the proposal is rejected, the Federal Parliament will have to find alternative solutions, potentially delaying the payment of the 13th pension.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## What to do as a cross-border commuter
In this crucial phase, it is important to understand your current pension status and how the vote on November 29 could influence your financial future. Cross-border commuters have concrete tools at their disposal to plan ahead.
### Check your personal AVS statement
The first step is to ensure you have a complete contribution history with the Swiss AVS. You can request a free statement from the territorial compensation office in your canton of work. This document shows all recorded contributions over the years and estimates the future pension based on contributions made up to that point. It is essential to verify that no contribution year has been omitted by mistake, as any gap reduces the final pension.
### Pension planning across multiple pillars
While awaiting the referendum result, cross-border commuters can plan their pension future by considering the second pillar (LPP - Swiss pension fund) and the third pillar (3a). These components are independent of the AVS and provide crucial additional protection. Many cross-border commuters do not fully utilize the contribution possibilities of the third pillar, which offers tax advantages both in Switzerland and Italy through the Italian tax credit.
The third pillar allows for tax-deductible annual contributions: a long-term strategy that protects against regulatory uncertainties such as those surrounding AVS funding.
### Timeline of next steps
The vote is scheduled for November 29. Cross-border commuters will receive official information from their canton of work and the municipalities of residence in Italy. In the event of approval, the VAT increase will come into effect according to the details communicated by the federal authorities. In the event of rejection, the debate on AVS funding will continue in the federal and cantonal parliamentary bodies.
### Available digital tools
Use the [paycheck calculator](nav:calculator) to check the impact of various scenarios on your tax deductions and AVS contributions. With a [pension simulation tool](nav:pension), you can plan different pension scenarios considering possible changes in the funding system. These calculations will allow you to make informed decisions about contributions to the third pillar and your overall pension strategy.
*Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/assemblea-centro%3a-s%c3%ac-a-finanziamento-avs-con-iva/92009988)*

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Varese Fair 2026: from September 11 to 20 at Schiranna. - 150 exhibitors and 40 events between sports, culture and businesses. - Edition's slogan: 'I choose Varese'.
## Key facts - **What**: 48th edition of Varese Fair - When: September 11-20, 2026 - Where: Schiranna exhibition area, Varese - Who: Deputy Mayor Ivana Perusin, Mayor Davide Galimberti - Exhibitors: About 150 - Surface: 5,000 square meters - Events: Over 40 between conferences and workshops
The 48th edition of the Varese Fair is preparing to open its doors at the Schiranna area, confirming its role as a reference point for the economic and social fabric of the territory. The event, scheduled from September 11 to 20, 2026, will take place on an exhibition area of 5,000 square meters, hosting about 150 exhibitors mainly from the Varesotto area. The event, which last year recorded over 60,000 visitors, aims this year to consolidate a model of aggregation that goes far beyond the traditional commercial exhibition. The chosen slogan for the current edition, 'I choose Varese', serves as a guiding thread for the entire duration of the event, representing a commitment to the enhancement of businesses, professionals, and local associative realities. Deputy Mayor Ivana Perusin emphasized how the fair has become a place of community capable of representing the many facets of the city, including in the program not only small and medium-sized businesses but also moments dedicated to culture, sports, and public debate.
### A multidisciplinary program The fair's offer is structured in six thematic areas that reflect the evolution of the event. The calendar includes over 40 appointments ranging from sector conferences, such as the one dedicated to urban security and the protection of local commerce titled 'Safe Commerce, Stronger Territories', to meetings on the role of journalism in the era of social media. There will also be technical insights, including a conference on artificial intelligence applied to businesses and sessions dedicated to slow tourism under the title 'Varese to Walk All Year Round'. The variety of the offer is designed to involve different segments of the public, integrating proposals on health, such as the meeting dedicated to osteoporosis, with moments of evening entertainment and stand-up comedy shows, confirming the transformation of the fair into a multifunctional container. The structural evolution of the Varese Fair, which shifts from a simple commercial showcase to a true hub of comparison, reflects the changes taking place in the Territorial Government Plan. According to the statements of Mayor Davide Galimberti, the event aims to be a moment of synthesis between the different components of society, integrating citizens, economic activities, tourism, and solidarity. This approach aligns with the desire to promote the quality of public spaces and urban development, themes that also closely touch the border territory. The event thus becomes a lens through which to observe the dynamics of transformation of the Varesotto area, a region that maintains strong ties with cross-border work activities. In the summer of 1911, miners and steelmakers crossed their arms for months. Workers from other parts of Italy came to their aid. Including Gallarate, with the combative figure of the trade unionist Ines Oddone Bittelli. In August 1911, a group of children from the area of Piombino and Elba arrived in Gallarate. It is not a holiday of pleasure (tourism, for the most part, does not yet exist) but a temporary and necessary migration: children of striking workers are welcomed in Gallarate as a form of help to their families who are struggling. Leading the arrival of the little Tuscans in and around Gallarate was Ines Oddone, a determined trade unionist, journalist on 'The class struggle', champion of women's and children's rights, wife of the secretary of the Chamber of Labour Giovanni Bitelli. The foster care of the 'children of the serrati' will involve about two hundred children. ## In brief - The Joint Commission has approved the Resolution on differentiated autonomy. - The Resolution concerns health, civil protection, professions, and social security. - The Regional Council will continue the negotiation process with the State.
## Key facts - **What**: Approval of the Resolution on differentiated autonomy. - When: September 2, 2026. - Where: Palazzo Pirelli, Milan. - Who: Special Commission “Autonomy and reorganization of local autonomies” and Commission for Institutional Affairs and Local Entities. - Amount: Not specified.
The Special Commission “Autonomy and reorganization of local autonomies” and the Commission for Institutional Affairs and Local Entities held a joint session at Palazzo Pirelli on September 2, 2026, to vote on the Resolution on differentiated autonomy. The Resolution, approved by a majority, mandates the Regional Council to continue the negotiation process with the State. The texts at the center of the vote concern the final agreement frameworks agreed with the Government, namely the attribution of additional competences and functions to the Lombardy Region in non-LEP matters (“civil protection”, “professions”, “complementary and supplementary social security”) and in the matter of “health protection – coordination of public finance”.
### Reactions of the Presidents The President of the Special Commission on Autonomy, Giovanni Malanchini (Lega), stated: “I am very satisfied with a process that has lasted three and a half years and will see its concluding act next week with the final vote in the Assembly. Regardless of all political positions, I want to thank all the commissioners for the relationship of loyal and correct collaboration that has characterized these years. Our work has always been based on total transparency and openness to dialogue with the minorities, carving out for the Commission a role entirely independent and autonomous from the Council, guaranteeing and protecting the centrality of the Regional Council. Thanks to this process, we arrive at a framework of functions that will allow Lombardy to respond with greater promptness, efficiency, and subsidiarity to the needs of citizens and businesses.”
The President of the Commission for Institutional Affairs, Matteo Forte (FdI), shared the same view, emphasizing the significance of the approved directive: “We are facing an important moment that is the outcome of solid work but represents a starting point and not an end. Differentiated autonomy is a dynamic process: with this Resolution, we give a clear mandate to the Council to continue the dialogue on further competences. What we approve is a necessary tool to ensure greater proximity of institutions to the needs of the territories.”
During today’s session, an amendment presented by Councilor Onorio Rosati (AVS) was put to a vote and rejected by a majority. The amendment requested that “the contents of the 2024 Constitutional Court ruling No. 192 be sufficiently valued in the text of the Resolution, fully incorporating what is contained in the premises of the preintese between the Lombardy Region and the Government.”
A negative vote was also cast for the popular petition promoted by some associations (from the Associations Coordinamento per la Democrazia Costituzionale – Milan, Libertà e Giustizia – Milan Circle and Comitati per il ritiro di ogni autonomia differenziata – Lombardy) which had collected, by the end of 2025, through the online platform Open Petition, the signatures of over 1500 citizens and asked the regional representatives to interrupt the process on differentiated autonomy.
From the opposition benches, numerous Councilors intervened: Carlo Borghetti (PD), Emilio Del Bono (PD), Gian Mario Fragomeli (PD), Michela Palestra (Patto Civico), and Onorio Rosati (AVS), all agreeing on their opposition to the Resolution.
“This is an act of grave political and procedural coercion that completely empties the sovereignty and guiding role of the Regional Council,” commented the minority representatives. “It is unacceptable that the Council has reactivated the dialogue with the Government based on an act from 2017 that is now completely outdated after the Constitutional Court ruling and the reduction of competences from 23 to just 4 matters. The choice was made to accelerate unjustifiably without prior debate in the Assembly of this legislature, ignoring the obligation of a rigorous investigation and bypassing a true preventive involvement of local entities, which risk having to manage... The approval of the Resolution has significant implications for commuters who work in Lombardy and reside in Ticino. The greater regional autonomy could lead to changes in health policies, civil protection, and professions, which could directly affect the daily lives of commuters. For example, greater regional control over health policies could result in more efficient management of resources and better quality of services provided, also benefiting commuters who use the Lombard health system.

For example, a cross-border commuter who changes employers in Lugano, with an annual salary of 80,000 CHF, will continue to pay AVS contributions (8.4% of the salary) and LPP contributions (7% of the salary) without interruption.

It is important to verify that all documents are up-to-date and compliant with the new regulations. For example, a cross-border commuter residing in Mendrisio must update the residence certificate with the municipality within 14 days of the change of employer.

Residence certificate: Update the residence certificate with the municipality of residence. 3. Civil status certificate: Verify that the civil status certificate is up-to-date. 4. G permit: Request the renewal of the G permit from the Migration Office within 30 days of the change of employer. 5. Insurance contributions: Verify the continuity of AVS, LPP, and LAMal contributions with the new employer.

This could reduce the income tax from 18,000 CHF to 15,000 CHF.
### Practical advice - Consult a tax advisor: Before changing employers, it is advisable to consult a tax advisor to assess the tax and contribution implications. - Verify documents: Ensure that all documents are up-to-date and compliant with the new regulations. - Renew the G permit: Carry out the renewal of the G permit within 30 days of the change of employer.
### Conclusion Changing employers for single cross-border commuters in 2024 involves a series of procedures and tax and contribution implications. It is important to follow an operational checklist and consult a tax advisor to assess the specific implications of changing employers.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-step procedure 1. **G permit renewal**: Submit the required documents to the Cantonal Tax Office (UCC) and the Cantonal Population Office (UCP) within 30 days of changing employers.
